Theo: Heads-up: onboarding reranker-2026 shows ndcg@10 down ~1.9% on our online-sim dataset after we enabled candidate-dedupe-by-url. MRR barely changes. Posting quick notes.
Marta: Interesting. We added URL dedupe to reduce near-duplicate noise, right? Which dedupe key did you use?
Theo: canonical_url (normalized) w/ suffix-strip. Baseline (no-dedupe) ndcg@10=0.644 -> dedupe-on=0.632. mrr@10 baseline 0.512 -> 0.510.
Chris: That sounds like dedupe removed some distinct high-quality variants that the reranker used to prefer. Do we have per-query top1 swaps?
Theo: Yes, sampled 200 swaps: 60% of swaps are cases where baseline chose doc with same url but different section anchor (e.g., /guides/install#mac vs /guides/install#linux). Dedupe favored keeping the first-seen anchor and removed others.
Marta: For many short queries, anchors matter (they contain the exact answer). By canonicalizing URL we lost anchor granularity. Ops changed canonicalization to strip anchors to unify indexing.
Chris: So the candidate pool lost useful negative/positive variation. Two options: (1) dedupe on canonical_url but keep distinct anchors as separate candidates when anchor-specific content differs, or (2) keep dedupe but prefer keeping candidate with highest paragraph-level match score.
Theo: I ran quick ablations: a) dedupe-strip-anchor -> ndcg 0.632 b) dedupe-preserve-anchor-if-anchor_text_diff -> ndcg 0.639 c) no-dedupe -> 0.644. So b) recovers most of gap.
Marta: Good. Implementation detail: need fast anchor-text fingerprint (hash of anchor snippet) in index to decide dedupe-keep. Also add a rankbench check to report "anchor_loss" metric when dedupe is enabled.
Chris: Also watch out for privacy/duplicates: some pages purposely publish same content across anchors; keep dedupe then. We should compute anchor_text_jaccard and only preserve when jaccard < 0.7 (i.e., distinct).
Theo: Action items:
- Marty: add anchor-fingerprint to indexer and update dedupe rule (owner: Marta)
- Chris: add rankbench metric "anchor_loss_count" and a small unit test dataset to catch regressions (owner: Chris)
- Theo: re-run full-sample eval after change and post numbers
analytics-bot: "note: dedupe-change rolled to canary at 2026-03-22T10:12:00Z"
Marta: I'll prototype anchor fingerprint and push a canary patch. If we still see >1% ndcg drop after anchor-aware dedupe we'll consider rolling back.
Theo: Thanks team. Learned: dedupe heuristics can silently remove important granular candidates; add slice-focused checks (short-query anchor-sensitive) to onboarding checklist. :eyes:
